content: In biology, a system refers to a collection of organs that collaborate to perform a specific function. In mammals and other animals, including humans, these systems are integral to anatomy and physiology. Examples include the circulatory system, respiratory system, and nervous system, among others. Humans possess a variety of systems due to the complexity of their organism. These systems are extensively studied in the field of human anatomy. Many of these systems are also present in other animals. Circulatory System: This system is responsible for pumping and directing blood to and from the body and lungs. It includes the heart, blood, and blood vessels. Digestive System: This system facilitates the digestion and processing of food. It involves the salivary glands, esophagus, stomach, liver, gallbladder, pancreas, intestines, rectum, and anus. Endocrine System: This system enables communication within the body through hormones produced by endocrine glands. These glands include the hypothalamus, pituitary gland, pineal gland, thyroid, parathyroids, and adrenal glands. Integumentary System: This system consists of the skin, hair, and nails, which serve as a protective barrier for the body. Lymphatic System: This system is involved in the transfer of lymph between tissues and the bloodstream. It includes lymph, lymph nodes, and lymphatic vessels. It also encompasses the Immune System, which defends the body against pathogens using leukocytes, tonsils, adenoids, thymus, and spleen. Muscular System: This system enables movement through the contraction and relaxation of muscles. Nervous System: This system is responsible for collecting, transmitting, and processing information. It includes the brain, spinal cord, peripheral nerves, and associated structures. Reproductive System: This system includes the organs involved in reproduction. In females, these include the ovaries, fallopian tubes, uterus, vagina, and mammary glands. In males, these include the testes, vas deferens, seminal vesicles, prostate, and penis. Respiratory System: This system facilitates breathing and includes the pharynx, larynx, trachea, bronchi, lungs, and diaphragm. Skeletal System: This system provides structural support and protection for the body. It consists of bones, cartilage, ligaments, and tendons. Urinary System: This system is involved in maintaining fluid and electrolyte balance and the excretion of urine. It includes the kidneys, ureters, bladder, and urethra.
